This file is an explicit, citable correction layer over exactly two of its numeric fields, plus one descriptor, established by leg 249's independent exact-rational re-derivation. source_of_the_correction.method: exact rational arithmetic (fractions.Fraction), LDL^T over Q with a Haynsworth bordering for the rank-one border row; sigma_min is BRACKETED by bisecting on dyadic lambda for definiteness of A^T G_c A - lambda G_d, not measured -- no rounding enters the verdict
source_of_the_correction.status_of_249: ESCALATED; its branch was pushed but never merged to main.  Its findings are what this record carries.

corrections.verdict: PROVED WRONG, not merely re-measured differently
corrections.proof: The pencil A^T G_c A - lambda G_d at lambda = (0.09080465147034879)^2 is NOT positive definite in exact rational arithmetic.  sigma_min is therefore STRICTLY BELOW the banked value.  The verdict contains no floating-point step.
corrections.mechanism: leg 176's eigh-based whitening loses accuracy as the X Gram's condition number grows; its error against the exact enclosure grows monotonically along the ladder 8.3e-13 -> 1.5e-11 -> 1.8e-11 -> 1.5e-10 -> 3.8e-10, reaching 5.08e-07 at N = 512.  A Cholesky whitening of the same matrices agrees with the exact tier at every rung.
corrections.headline_unaffected: The quoted headline sigma_min = 0.0908 reproduces exactly.  Only the 7th significant figure onward is wrong.

corrections.mechanism: same eigh-whitening mechanism as K1; the banked N = 128 tail value is out by 3.7e-09 against its own exact enclosure.
corrections.headline_unaffected: The quoted headline ||T^{-1}||_X = 4.026 reproduces to all four figures it is quoted to.

corrections.banked_text: here it converges, ||T^{-1}||_X = 4.03 at K=2, truncation-independent.
corrections.verdict: The DESCRIPTOR 'truncation-independent' is FALSE at the precision the number is quoted to.  The VALUE 4.03 in this same reading field is the one the data support.

evidence.monotone: rising at every rung, still rising at N = 1024

corrections.correct_reading: A monotone sequence with geometrically shrinking decrements -- float64 evidence of a finite limit, not a proof of one, which is exactly the reading leg 176 gives its OTHER number.  The limit is approximately 4.0318, not 4.026.
corrections.note: Leg 176's own reading field already said 4.03; the journal and PUB2 tightened it to 4.026 on the way out, to a figure the data do not support.

what_is_NOT_corrected.leg_176_gate_answer: UNCHANGED and independently confirmed.  Leg 249 re-derived every matrix, identity and convergence claim from the definitions and all of them survive.
what_is_NOT_corrected.leg_176_conclusions: UNCHANGED: the formulation closes; sigma_min is bounded away from zero uniformly in the truncation; the tail inverse norm CONVERGES where ell^1_w's DIVERGED; Z_1 still fails at 140.72.
what_is_NOT_corrected.the_ell1w_contrast: UNAFFECTED.  It is a contrast between a converging sequence here and a diverging one there (legs 51/53).  Convergence to 4.0318 makes that contrast exactly as strong as convergence to 4.026 would -- which is why this is a precision-and-wording correction and not an escalation of PUB2's argument.
two_findings_that_strengthen_leg_176: Its reliable window is WIDER than it claimed: under a Cholesky whitening the sigma_min ladder is monotone decreasing through N = 2048.  The N = 1024 rise is a property of leg 176's eigh whitening, not of the X Gram's float floor.

Its Xu closed-form reproduction is 7.1x BETTER than its own residual metric reports: its banked 4.767e-15 measures its own floating-point residual assembly; against an exact evaluation its u(y) is correct to 6.74e-16.
what_is_NOT_corrected.convention_caveat_recorded_by_249: sigma_min is convention-relative: the X + C Gram puts unit weight on the border amplitude while the X block carries the bare Laguerre normalization.  Sweeping that weight over 10^-2..10^2 moves sigma_min across 0.01086..0.13580 (factor 12.5); adopting Xu's y-space normalization (carrying the 2 pi) gives 0.0420 instead of 0.0908.  The GATE property -- bounded away from zero uniformly in the truncation -- is invariant; the DIGITS are not.
